conditions: Applies to every ODD product over GTL/ABG.
concepts.definition: The profile's constructive homeostasis loop runs from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to the next lawful action. Its operative functions are synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action. It corrects toward required conditions as observations arrive, without guaranteeing convergence or the adequacy of those conditions.

grounding.quote:
it corrects towards the required conditions as observations arrive,
guarantees neither convergence nor the adequacy of those conditions, and
its diagnoses distinguish the four causes named there (P2, P6).

concepts.label: Constructive evaluation and yield loop

concepts.definition: Loop carrier vocabulary: IntentLineage is admitted source intent and lineage from a human, imported source, prior product, intent engine or prior synthesized construction intent, backed by ABG event-log truth. ProductAssetModel is desired and known typed asset truth synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth, with admitted-event and product-projection publication refs; it is neither runtime fact nor action authority. Worksite is the observable workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and file/process state. RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted runtime facts; RuntimeProjection is replay-derived runtime state over event log and execution basis. ObservationSnapshot is a read-only runtime/worksite view; GapPressureRow represents missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous asset/evidence pressure. TargetObligationBinding binds pressure to the exact selected outcome, admitted prerequisite/experiment basis, assets, roles, evidence and admissible outcomes. ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes. NextActionBasis is the dispatch sum initial_selection, post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice or post_block, not a controller. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible policy. ConstructionIntent is an admitted selected action for one bounded invocation preserving outcome/basis refs. AdmittedEvidence includes worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence, without worker self-closure. EdgeFulfillmentLedger carries evidence and convergence for one edge attempt/version. EdgeClosureDecision carries closure truth. NextActionProjection reads current truth and NextActionBasis and selects only when lawful.
exceptions: post_reprice carries a re-entry request and no action-selection authority.

grounding.quote: | `NextActionProjection` | Read model that observes `NextActionBasis` plus current truth and selects a next graph action only when lawful. | ABG next-action evaluation projection with product policy. |

| `TargetObligationBinding` | Exact binding from gap pressure to the selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs, and admissible graph outcomes. | Product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. |

concepts.label: Constructive loop carriers

concepts.definition: The selected Product outcome is external authority for the loop under SPEC_METHOD §3. An admitted bounded prerequisite or experiment can also supply a bounded work basis. Models, gaps, assurance, ledgers and projections interpret these bases but do not author, select or enlarge the outcome.

grounding.quote:
Product models, gaps, assurance, ledgers and
projections may interpret that outcome but cannot author, select or
enlarge it. `evaluate_next` may select material work only within that
outcome or within an admitted bounded prerequisite or experiment.

concepts.label: Selected outcome and admitted bounded basis

concepts.definition: Four separate authority functions: synthesize_model takes IntentLineage, prior ProductAssetModel and admitted product truth and produces ProductAssetModel; eval_gap takes ProductAssetModel, RuntimeEventLog, RuntimeProjection and Worksite and produces ObservationSnapshot and GapPressureRow; evaluate_next takes NextActionBasis, fresh eval_gap, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog and Policy and produces PriorityProjection, NextActionProjection and selected_action, plus its own core result for typed no-action; evaluate_action takes ConstructionIntent, AdmittedEvidence, TargetObligationBinding and Policy and produces EdgeFulfillmentLedger and EdgeClosureDecision.

grounding.quote:
The loop has one model-synthesis function and three distinct evaluation
functions. They may share underlying libraries; they must not share
authority (P6):

concepts.label: Model synthesis and three evaluation functions

concepts.definition: The governed work pair comprises mutable workspace W and immutable ledger L of closure-relevant work over W, anchored and ordered by immutable event spine E. Evaluator work Ev evaluates declared L snapshots. L records admitted callout basis, observed deltas, file refs, digests, execution evidence, touched obligations, claims, evaluator inputs/outputs and admission status, rather than copying W. Ledger attention is a structural analogy: typed, immutable, lineage-constrained, policy-bounded and replayable, without a transformer-attention implementation dependency.

grounding.quote:
F_P acts in W.
Admission records governed facts in L.
E orders and anchors L entries with predecessor refs.
Ev evaluates a declared L snapshot, not ambient W.
Ev output is itself F_P work and is admitted back into L/E.

concepts.label: Workspace, ledger and evaluator attention

concepts.definition: The closed closure-decision vocabulary is close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice and block. These evaluate the predicate that the edge's obligations are fulfilled on the exact basis. Cause refinements map each refined value to exactly one core result without adding decisions or core values. Selection results evaluate whether a published lawful action can be selected for the current gap on the exact basis. Candidate availability, candidate acceptance and edge fulfillment are distinct predicates; ACTIVATION acceptance dispositions accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject are not closure decisions.

grounding.quote:
A closure decision is not a disposition and is never recorded
as one, and no disposition is a closure decision: `repair` is not
`local_repair`, and `re-enter` is not `re_enter`. Edge closure is
evidence toward acceptance and never acceptance itself

concepts.label: Closure, selection, availability and acceptance results

concepts.definition: ODD supplies structural product shape; each domain product owns its asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays. The same structural law can build different domain products.

grounding.quote:
This profile gives the product shape, not the domain semantics. The same
ODD structural law can build many different domain products, and each
product defines its own asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays.
Structural GTL law and product-specific semantic law are never confused
(P1).

concepts.label: Structural profile and product semantic law

conditions: The operator uses only declared authority surfaces.
concepts.definition: A manual walkthrough identifies current asset/node state, the next lawful vector and its public graph-function carrier, required inputs/evaluators/output contract/carried environment, constructs or assesses the next asset/checkpoint, and repeats to target-relative closure. A vector is the constitutional transition contract; its graph function is the published constructive program realizing it.
concepts.label: Lawful manual traversal

concepts.definition: Agentic conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough proves the constitutional process can be followed on real work from declared authority, and an F_D deterministic gate admits produced artifacts. The walkthrough covers intake triage, smallest lawful re-entry, specification/requirement/design/ticket chain, constructive evaluation and closure proof. A minimal authority packet carries input/output contract, required context, role, evaluator regime, provenance and the smallest sufficient declared authority with source refs.

grounding.quote:
Conformance has two halves: an F_P proof that the process can be followed,
and an F_D gate that admits the produced artifacts (P6).

concepts.label: Agentic walkthrough and artifact admission

conditions: Applies to an ODD or graph-native boundary.
concepts.definition: Real authority-path negative proof exercises the supported Product authority path. Closure-grade evidence identifies entry and authority, invalidates the actual authority-bearing input, exercises that path, proves refusal before the prohibited effect and establishes that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence are distinct claims.

grounding.quote:
Closure-grade negative evidence identifies the supported entry and the
governing authority; invalidates the real authority-bearing input;
exercises the supported path; proves refusal before the prohibited
effect; and establishes that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or
parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence
are distinct claims (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Real authority-path negative proof

concepts.definition: Graph composition uses a cumulative typed environment. A later function can require any typed binding available in that carried environment. Each retained GraphFunction should declare environment.requires, environment.provides and environment.carries.

grounding.quote:
Each retained `GraphFunction` should declare `environment.requires`,
`environment.provides` and `environment.carries`. A later function may
require any typed binding available in the cumulative carried
environment, not only the immediately previous output (P4a, P4b).

concepts.label: Cumulative typed environment

concepts.definition: Global convergence requires lawful inner closure, preservation of the enclosing coarse contract after fold-back and agreement between zoomed and unzoomed open/closed status. Current requirement proof is proof-lane aware: a governed realized witness appropriate to the requirement class is required; realized testcases or archived test evidence are the usual immediate pressure for an active software line.

grounding.quote:
When an outer public carrier is refined
into inner executable structure, the refined inner chain must close
lawfully; the enclosing coarse contract must also stay true after
fold-back; and zoomed and unzoomed views must agree on whether the
enclosing carrier is open or closed (P4a, P2).

concepts.label: Global convergence under refinement

concepts.definition: Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces. A bundle should identify the exercised feature/use-case boundary, pre-existing assets, expected vectors, significant paths and closure evidence. Declared scenarios and use cases are preferred sources for selecting significant code/control proving paths because they pressure feature intent and design decisions.

grounding.quote:
Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces, not only test
documentation. A scenario bundle should make clear which feature or
use-case boundary is exercised; which assets are expected to exist before
the scenario starts; which vectors are expected to be traversed; which
significant paths are expected to be exercised; and what evidence closes
the scenario (P2, P6).

concepts.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The product has an installable development form.
concepts.definition: Installed-development proof is decisive proof run against that installed form in isolation. For graph-native ODD products the proving lane should exercise installation, project bootstrap, graph traversal, evidence collection and target-relative closure. ASSURANCE §5 owns this rule.

grounding.quote:
Where the product has an installable development form, decisive proof
runs against that installed development form in an isolated environment.
For a graph-native ODD product the proving lane should exercise install,
project bootstrap, graph traversal, evidence collection and
target-relative closure. Direct source checks stay useful and do not
replace installed-dev proof (P6, P3). This rule is the profile's binding of
[ASSURANCE §5 Installed dev proof](ASSURANCE.md#5-installed-dev-proof), which
owns it.

concepts.label: Installed-dev proof

concepts.definition: ODD dogfooding is development through the graph-native method the product provides, increasingly using explicit assets, vectors, graph functions, scenario bundles and target-relative closure.

grounding.quote:
The project should therefore increasingly describe and
build itself through explicit assets, explicit vectors, explicit graph
functions, explicit scenario bundles and explicit target-relative closure.

concepts.label: ODD dogfooding

concepts.definition: Release versions belong to release process/metadata, not constitutional graph truth. Graph-native method concerns current assets, vectors, closures and authority; immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut acceptance belong to the separate RELEASE process surface.

grounding.quote:
A release version is not constitutional graph truth; it belongs to the
release process and release metadata. The graph-native method concerns
current assets, current vectors, current closures and current authority.
Immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut
acceptance stay a separate process surface, [RELEASE](RELEASE.md) (P3,
P6).

concepts.label: Graph truth and release process boundary

conditions: An agent or designer is instructed to build a product using ODD.
concepts.definition: The expected invocation sequence is: read SPEC_METHOD; read an existing product-specific method; read local Intent, Product, relevant requirements and active design; identify source-to-outcome semantic chain, typed assets and public graph functions; define the machine-readable catalogue; define/update GTL outer callable carriers and live traversal boundaries; define scale-consistent coarse/inner/proof closure; complete the execution-authority audit for affected runtime/plugin/worker/event/projection/assurance/closure/continuation surfaces; define the constructive loop and closure vocabulary including lawful yield; define projection/query over admitted history with source coherence; only then implement code, policy and transport.

grounding.quote:
13. define the projection and query lane as a projection over admitted
    constructive history, including the structural coherence rule between
    the read model and its source carrier;
14. only then implement code, policy and transport surfaces.

concepts.label: ODD product-authoring sequence

conditions: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product.
concepts.definition: Cold-start reading is ordered. General route: SPEC_METHOD; ODD; product stdo_<label>.json; applicable bound project reference-frame basis and authorized activation packet; bound Intent; bound Product; relevant bound requirements; active bound design; GTL module, catalogue and queries. World-model route inserts WORLD_MODEL after ODD, uses relevant bound requirement families and current bound design, and includes the proof lane with the final GTL/catalogue/query surfaces. ODD sets structural expectations, the product method sets domain law and local surfaces set the current build line. Skipping the order usually risks missing domain meaning or realizing it through the wrong carrier.

grounding.quote: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product, read in the order below (P1, P2).
9. the GTL module, function catalogue and query surfaces.
10. the GTL module, function catalogue, query surfaces and proof lane.

concepts.label: General and world-model cold-start routes

concepts.definition: ODD's canonical compression describes graph-native GTL/ABG product authoring: typed assets, named functions, published catalogue, operative GTL module, ABG execution authority, one constructive loop, current-state projections over constructive history, lawful manual explainability, outcome-first framework realization and agentic walkthrough plus deterministic admission. It is a derived acquisition surface with no determination of its own; its declared sources are same-digest §§1, 2, 11.1–11.5D, 11.7 and 11.7A.

grounding.quote:
This section is a compression of this member, a derived surface in the
sense of [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition. Its sources are §1, §2, §11.1 to §11.5D, §11.7 and §11.7A of
this member at the same digest, and it owns no determination. Where it and
a source section differ, the source section decides

concepts.label: ODD derived canonical compression

concepts.definition: POSTING_GUIDE owns the governed project's commentary layer: post purpose, authority boundary, location, identity, categories, structure, discussion state, posting rules and ratification. It consumes PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 ticketing.comments, TICKETS §1 work carriers, SPEC_METHOD §2 authority surfaces and EVALUATION §1 claims/evidence without redefining them; SPEC_METHOD §6 owns shared-method adoption. Clauses cite FOUNDATIONS principles P0–P6.

grounding.quote:
Guide. Owns the commentary layer of a governed project: what a post is
for, its boundary with authority, where posts live, their identity,
categories and structure, their discussion state, the posting rules and
ratification. Consumes

concepts.label: POSTING_GUIDE

concepts.definition: A post is working commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff or repricing confidence. It may influence later specification/design but is not constitutional truth. Its category is one of REVIEW (critique), STRATEGY (proposed technical/method direction), GAP (precise insufficiency/contradiction), SCHEMA (data/event/interface/contract shape), HANDOFF (bounded context/task-state transfer) or MATRIX (explicit decision-option comparison).

grounding.quote:
A post is not constitutional truth. It is working commentary, and it may
later influence specification or design (P6).

concepts.label: Post and category vocabulary

concepts.definition: A post carrier is bound by ticketing.comments.root, defaulting locally to .ai-workspace/comments/<agent>/. Default file identity is YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS_CATEGORY_SUBJECT.md; 20260327T120000_REVIEW_bootloader-boundary.md is an example, not a required post. Non-file carriers preserve equivalent stable identity, publication time, category, subject, author, discussion state and supersession history.

grounding.quote:
Posts live at the location the product definition binds as
`ticketing.comments.root` (P6, P3). The default local-file
binding is:

A carrier that is not a file must preserve an equivalent stable post
identity, publication time, category, subject, author, discussion state
and supersession history (P3, P4b).

concepts.label: Commentary carrier and post identity

concepts.definition: The post template has title CATEGORY: Subject; Author; ISO 8601 Date; Addresses identifying the artifact/issue/boundary; Status initially Draft; optional ISO 8601 Updated; Summary; Analysis; and Recommended Action. MATRIX uses a central decision table instead of free prose. Discussion states are Draft (author shaping), Open (published active discussion) and Closed (discussion concluded).
concepts.label: Post structure and discussion state

concepts.definition: PRODUCT_DEFINITION is a tier-2 member owning project binding through the overlay, definition relations, constitutional-set sufficiency, installed release/toolchain management, semantic resolution, local binding, collective frame basis, WHAT/HOW/work carriers, discovery/composition, conformance cases, STDO-SURFACE-001 and bootstrap. It consumes tier-1 FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION without adding tier-1 definitions. Its contexts are product-definition-routing (§§1–4, 9, 12), semantic-resolution (§§5, 6, 10) and build-tenancy (§8). Generic WHAT/HOW, lineage, build-tenant, release and assurance law remain with the cited owners. Its schemas/templates/filenames/fields/commands are Product realization shapes accepted as interoperability boundaries, not profile terms.

grounding.quote:
The schemas, templates, filenames, manifest
fields and commands named here are this Product's own realisation shapes,
accepted as interoperability boundaries under §11; they are not profile
terms. Three bounded contexts are
owned here: product-definition-routing (§1 to §4, §9, §12),
semantic-resolution (§5, §6, §10) and build-tenancy (§8).

concepts.label: PRODUCT_DEFINITION member

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
concepts.definition: The product-definition-routing context, urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing, owns overlay, definition, discovery, locator and composition meanings. A product definition is a JSON locator/relation overlay for one continuing product WHAT, independent of existing layout. Its definition root is its containing directory; relative URI references resolve against the definition file's retrieval URI. product.source_project locates a source-project root that may be elsewhere. The conventional filename is stdo_<label>.json, with stdo_default.json the single-definition source-project default.

grounding.quote:
This member owns the product-definition-routing bounded context,
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing`, under the selected
complete STDO basis, and defines that context's overlay, definition,
discovery, locator and composition concepts. The JSON schema named below
realises the accepted interoperability shape of the overlay and is not a
second semantic owner (P6).

concepts.label: Product definition overlay

concepts.definition: Definition Label is a stable lowercase ASCII-letter/digit/hyphen/underscore discovery label unique only within a directory, not Product identity. Product-Definition Identity is product.definition_id, a stable URI for the mutable definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition set. Immutable Products/releases retain separate identities. The normative JSON schema is schemas/product-definition.schema.json and the single fill-in form is templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json; they standardize identity/location/relation/discovery fields without absorbing referenced meaning.

grounding.quote:
The suffix `<label>` is the Definition Label: a stable lowercase local
discovery label of ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique
only among the definitions in the same directory. It is not Product
identity. The `product.definition_id` URI inside the definition is the
Product-Definition Identity: the stable identity of the mutable
product-definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition
set. It identifies one continuing WHAT definition, not one immutable
released Product (P3).

concepts.label: Definition identities, schema and template

concepts.definition: F12 traces project-binding rules to foundational commitments plus instance premises: independent project authorities; chosen existing layout; shared workspace/machine; recurring terms with different context meanings; and immutable released method versions selected, installed and replaced by projects. P1, P2, P3 and P6 are independent; P0 is recovered; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with the premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable. The family traces imports without owning that law, distinguishes consequences from member-owned interoperability/domain choices and supplies a per-row consumer-locus index.

grounding.quote:
The index also assigns to this family the rule of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members);
the table traces that rule in its sixth row, whose rule column names that
section, and owns none of it. Each commitment's standing is written as the
table of commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

concepts.label: F12 foundation-to-law family

concepts.definition: A Constitutional Set is the complete selected governing document set for a product, with no prescribed file count. It collectively makes recoverable axioms (starting truths, invariants, refusal conditions), ontology (real kinds, identities, relations, boundaries, lifecycle), epistemology (evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification, acceptability and decision authority), taxonomy (classifications preventing category collapse), and semantics (governed meanings of terms, relations, states, operations and outcomes). These are sufficiency dimensions, not filename classes or folders.

grounding.quote:
A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1):

concepts.label: Constitutional Set

conditions: Within product-definition-routing.
concepts.definition: Installed Release Basis is the pair of immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI and installed-manifest SHA-256. The URI identifies an annotated immutable RC cut; the deterministic manifest binds tag object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. Its schema is schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json. The manifest is transport/integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution.

grounding.quote:
The URI identifies one immutable annotated RC cut. The digest identifies
the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).

concepts.label: Installed Release Basis

concepts.definition: An Adoption Plan is a read-only deterministic acceptance object binding current Product Definition identity/bytes/current basis to one resolved immutable target cut, tag object, commit, tree and manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is an operator-presentable acceptance token, whose possession alone grants no authority. A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorized fleet root and the complete ordered per-definition plan-digest set.

grounding.quote:
Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

concepts.label: Adoption and Fleet Adoption Plans

concepts.definition: The STDO Toolchain Manager is a bounded executable realization that installs each immutable cut once in a shared versioned store, resolves logical release URIs to verified bytes, inventories/verifies complete distributions, synchronizes selected exact bases, plans and explicitly acceptedly performs adoption, manages declared marker-bounded agent bootstrap and applies operations to an explicitly discovered fleet. The store registry maps release URIs to paths/digests and owns neither Product selection nor method meaning.

grounding.quote:
- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a mutable version-line
  selector and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly
  accepted;
- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and
- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product
  Definitions.

concepts.label: STDO Toolchain Manager

concepts.definition: A Complete Consumer Update Plan binds one explicitly selected Product Definition and the complete companion population of one exact upstream release-matched cohort to owner-selected consumer bindings. Its invocation/plan/result are operation evidence, not a persistent dependency declaration, registry or lock. cohort-update presents a whole plan binding effect destinations, preimages, exact cohort bytes, companion tags/commits/subtrees/inventories, replacement dependency locators, native routes and declared derived-source observations. Product Definition owns composition; upstream cohort and Product release records own release/member identities.

grounding.quote:
The caller selects every native route and derived context
for the claimed update scope; directory proximity or an empty discovery
result cannot supply that selection, and an empty derived-context
population means the owner selected none, not that the manager established
the absence of semantic context (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Complete consumer update

concepts.definition: Toolchain outcomes are cause-refined core results for separate predicates: external effect occurrence; lawful admission/activation on an exact subject and basis; candidate availability after commencement; and a read-only command's own evaluated condition. Completion status, effect-end establishment, refusal cause and partial effects remain distinct data.

grounding.quote:
Outcomes as results. The outcomes of the manager's operations in §4,
its refusals, its reported completion and the recovery that
loss requires, are stated in the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) through the refinements
of [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition), each
for its own predicate; the cause of an outcome selects its value, and the
mapping adds no core value (P5, P6):

concepts.label: Toolchain effect and refusal result domains

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
concepts.definition: Semantic-resolution law is owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution. A term is a lexical label in an occurrence. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope whose vocabulary, concepts and relations are jointly interpretable under named authority. A concept reference exactly locates an authority-owned meaning on a selected basis without minting meaning or authority. Every material occurrence's semantic address is (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope).

grounding.quote:
A term is a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept
identity. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope in
which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly
interpretable under named authority. A concept reference is an exact,
resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected
basis; the reference locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor
its authority (P1, P3, P6).

concepts.label: Bounded-context semantic resolution

concepts.definition: Four owner-authorized cross-context relation kinds: Semantic Import applies unchanged source meaning in declared target scope under FOUNDATIONS import law; Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import; Semantic Equivalence is an equality established by governing authorities while both concepts retain owners/contexts and neither adopts the other's meaning; Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating alternatives, using a declared import/translation/equivalence if the selected meaning is external. Specialisation is directional translation preserving declared source meaning while narrowing admissible instances or adding target constraints.

grounding.quote:
A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the
declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding
target-context constraints. It identifies the exact target concept, the
preserved and narrowed meaning, the excluded source instances, and the
absence or law of any inverse. Calling a term a specialisation without
those coordinates establishes nothing (P1, P3).

concepts.label: Semantic relations and specialisation

concepts.definition: Local constitutional entries locate local axioms, overrides and disambiguations whose authority belongs to an existing lawful owner. A local disambiguation carrier owns the resolution; overlay metadata only makes its exact context, candidates, selected concept, bases, authority and scope discoverable/checkable.

grounding.quote:
The referenced `uri` owns the resolution. When the candidates cross bounded
contexts, that carrier also declares the complete import, translation or
equivalence relation §5 requires. The overlay metadata makes the relation
discoverable and checkable; it neither restates the source-owned meanings
nor mints the decision (P6).

concepts.label: Local constitutional binding

concepts.definition: A Project Reference-Frame Basis is a Product-owned accepted declaration of the shared frame set through which finite actors engage a governed scope/outcome. It binds exact frame law and optional profile basis, admitting authorities/scopes, frame declarations/evaluation inventory, actor-binding rules/capability envelopes, semantic/evaluation/operation/decision grants, result/conjunction/translation/coverage relations, lifecycle triggers and invalidation. REFERENCE_FRAME supplies principles/declaration shape and the Executive baseline supplies an optional profile; Product authority owns the concrete declaration and every grant.

grounding.quote:
Project Reference-Frame Basis
  = exact reference-frame law and optional profile basis
  + admitting authorities and governed scopes
  + frame declarations and evaluation inventory
  + actor-binding rules and capability envelopes
  + semantic, evaluation, operation and decision grants
  + result, conjunction, translation and coverage relations
  + lifecycle activation triggers and invalidation law
```

concepts.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

concepts.definition: Agent Frame Activation is an execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable frame/configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope. Its packet is carried by a ticket or other authorized work instruction, while the Product Definition locates the durable shared frame basis. Profile availability, Product adoption and execution activation are distinct relations.

grounding.quote:
Profile availability, Product adoption and execution-scoped activation are
three distinct relations. Inclusion in a selected method cut makes a
profile available; only Product authority may adopt it; only an exact
authorised work instruction may activate one bound frame for an actor and
subject (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Agent Frame Activation

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
concepts.definition: The build-tenancy context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy. Build tenancy is one constitutional WHAT realized by one or more independent project-owned HOW tenants: one is the singleton case; multiple independent realizations of the same WHAT constitute multi-build-tenancy. SPEC_METHOD §11 owns build-tenant meanings/bindings, and TICKETS §4 owns the multi-tenant work-item relation through explicit owner relations.

grounding.quote:
In this context build tenancy is that one-or-more relation; one tenant is
its singleton case, and multi-build-tenancy begins when the same WHAT has
more than one independent realisation (P3, P2).

concepts.label: Build tenancy

concepts.definition: Tenant Registry is canonical how.build_tenants, identifying independent HOW realizations by stable identity and locating roots/design/implementation; tenant surfaces declare bindings under SPEC_METHOD §11. how.common locates common realization law explicitly adopted across multiple tenants. WHAT bindings locate current Intent, Product and specifications. ticketing.goals locates the work wave; ticketing.tickets locates durable tickets with backlog/active/completed lanes; ticketing.comments locates commentary; optional ticketing.sprints locates bounded execution-batch manifests.

grounding.quote:
The Tenant Registry is the canonical `how.build_tenants` collection for the
product's independent HOW realisations. Each entry has stable identity and
locates its root, design and implementation surfaces; the tenant's
binding, which those surfaces declare, is governed by SPEC_METHOD §11.
The Common Build-Tenant Surface is the realisation law bound by `how.common` and
explicitly adopted across more than one tenant. A separate
`TENANT_REGISTRY.md` may remain as a human-readable companion or generated
projection and cannot become a second tenant-identity or location
authority (P3, P6).

concepts.label: WHAT, tenant registry and work-carrier bindings

exceptions: Further material work requires another admitted basis after a terminal or exhausted basis.

grounding.quote:
The loop selects no further material work without another admitted basis
once the selected outcome is accepted; an admitted prerequisite is
discharged; an admitted experiment's stated decision is resolved; another
admitted terminal condition is reached; or its governing basis or bound
is exhausted, rejected, withdrawn, superseded, repriced away or
falsified. A `reprice` disposition requests lawful constitutional
re-entry; it neither performs the reprice nor selects the successor
outcome (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Material work must remain within the selected outcome or an admitted bounded prerequisite/experiment. No further material selection occurs after outcome acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment decision resolution, another admitted terminal condition, or exhaustion/rejection/withdrawal/supersession/repricing-away/falsification of its basis or bound without another admitted basis. Reprice requests constitutional re-entry; it performs neither repricing nor successor-outcome selection. Graph/edge closure is evidence toward Product acceptance, never Product or release acceptance.

grounding.quote:
No CLI branch, prompt prose, postflight string, gap-dossier action list,
query projection, service method or local operator summary may become a
rival source of traversal truth (P6).

constraints.statement: Every GTL/ABG ODD product must preserve one authoritative traversal-consequence surface: IntentLineage → ProductAssetModel → ObservationSnapshot → GapPressureRow → TargetObligationBinding → PriorityProjection → ConstructionIntent → AdmittedEvidence → EdgeFulfillmentLedger → EdgeClosureDecision → NextActionProjection, with selected outcome/admitted bounded-basis refs also feeding TargetObligationBinding. No CLI branch, prompt, postflight string, gap-dossier list, query, service or operator summary may rival it. Carrier renaming cannot alter this authority shape.

exceptions: Libraries may be shared; authority may not.

grounding.quote:
A module that lets one of these
functions exercise another's authority creates a rival control surface
and violates A0 (P6).

constraints.statement: synthesize_model may update desired/known typed asset truth only from event-backed lineage, prior model and admitted product truth; it cannot observe worksite, admit intent, invoke, close or select work. eval_gap only observes and emits gap pressure; it cannot admit intent, invoke, close or choose work. evaluate_action only folds admitted action evidence into ledger and closure decision; it cannot select the next graph action. evaluate_next may bind obligations, rank lawful published actions and publish next-action projection, but cannot admit intent or decide prior-action closure/yield/failure/repair except by consuming admitted EdgeClosureDecision. Designs, tickets, modules and proofs must identify the specific implemented/consumed function rather than merely say evaluator.

conditions: Before every constructive action invocation.
exceptions: The admitted prerequisite/experiment reference is optional when the selected outcome alone is the basis.

grounding.quote:
`ConstructionIntent` must cite the lineage, the
selected action and the `TargetObligationBinding` that preserve the exact
selected Product outcome and any admitted bounded-basis refs (P4b, P6).

A3 Published action law. `evaluate_next` may rank only published lawful
actions from the action catalogue. If the desired action is unpublished,
the lawful result is a typed no-action disposition, not a fallback to a
broad executive graph or a local script (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Bind current gap, exact target assets, obligations, required roles and evidence refs to the exact selected outcome and any admitted prerequisite/experiment before invocation. A broad edge satisfies a specific gap only if the binding proves its lawfulness for those assets. External/bootstrap intent seeds the model but cannot invent unpublished actions. After evaluate_next selects an already-published function/vector, a distinct admission step admits construction intent synthesized against model and gap, citing lineage, selected action and preserving target-binding authority refs. An unpublished desired action yields typed no-action, never a broad-graph/script fallback.

grounding.quote:
Every closure-relevant F_P callout that does work needs ledger admission.
Evaluator work is not outside F_P merely because it reads ledgers: it is
F_P work over governed ledger state, and its result must be admitted into
the immutable ledger and event spine before it can affect closure, routing
or traversal. Corrections append or supersede ledger and event facts; they
do not rewrite the governed history of work (P4b, P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Filesystem/process output, screen logs, worker artifacts and product files are observations, gaining authority only through typed evidence admission and folding into ledger/decision truth. W may change without being true; L may be true without containing all W. Closure and evaluation judge W only through L, and evaluator outputs affect traversal only after their own L/E admission. Every closure-relevant F_P callout needs admission; corrections append/supersede rather than rewrite history. Evaluators may attend only to admitted rows reachable through declared lineage, predecessor refs, target binding, policy and relevant event cursor; outside workspace facts, prose, archives, summaries and controller memory are excluded. Closure cannot follow raw artifact presence, worker report, process success or CLI summary. The fulfillment ledger records counts, obligation rows, materialization/liveness/admission refs and edge_converged; it never selects the next action.

exceptions: Unresolved post_reprice must return no_action(undeclared) pending separately admitted constitutional re-entry.

grounding.quote:
On `post_reprice`, `evaluate_next` must return a typed no-action
disposition while constitutional re-entry stays unresolved. The reprice
decision cannot authorise a replacement action; work may be evaluated
again only after lawful re-entry separately admits an exact selected
Product outcome or bounded basis and supplies it through a new
`initial_selection` or a basis-bearing resume. Default graph following is
ordinary, but it is still an `evaluate_next` decision and not hidden
sequential control (P5, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: evaluate_next must be total. initial_selection uses current model/gap/binding/catalogue/policy. post_yield_resume resumes or yields the same lawful edge from replay-visible resume truth without failure classification. post_close_graph_continuation may choose the next edge or empty selection when complete. For post_retry/post_repair/post_reenter/post_block, select a higher-priority lawful action if one exists; otherwise follow the current edge if lawful; otherwise if authority is missing return a reprice-or-block typed no-action; otherwise block with typed no-action. These are selection outcomes, not evaluate_action closure decisions. Default following still passes through evaluate_next. Post-reprice work can be evaluated again only after separately admitted exact outcome/bounded basis enters new initial_selection or basis-bearing resume.

exceptions: An earlier result stands for no-action only if it decided the same selection predicate on the current basis.

grounding.quote:
Where the graph is complete and no action follows a closed edge, nothing
is refused and no selection determination is made: the empty selection is
invocational data, and `close` keeps its own value for the edge predicate
under A8.

constraints.statement: Selected next action is invocational data, not a core result. Each typed no-action independently answers whether a lawful published action can be selected for this gap on this exact basis, retaining its domain outcome beside its core value. no_action(undeclared) maps to out_of_frame when catalogue lacks the action or no admitted basis declares a needed relation/capability/authority; it names the missing item and owner. no_action(basis) maps to invalid_basis when the current outcome/catalogue/policy cannot support the gap. On unresolved post_reprice, no_action(undeclared) names the undeclared outcome/bound and declaring re-entry. Prior closure results are selection evidence only and neither predicate's value counts toward the other. A next-action projection establishes availability only. Empty selection after a closed, complete graph is neither refusal nor selection determination.

conditions: Closure results use admitted evidence and exact edge basis.
exceptions: For re-enter or block with both undeclared and basis causes, record both and take the basis value.

grounding.quote:
A decision with both causes records both and takes the
`basis` value, as
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
decides for `re_entry_requested`.

| `repair(implementation)` | falsified | the failing obligation row is the counterexample (P5, P6) |
| `repair(proof)` | indeterminate | the defect is in the proof, so the admitted evidence cannot decide the obligation; the decision's reason refs name the repaired proof that would decide (P5, P6) |

constraints.statement: Every closure decision is replay-visible with sufficient basis/reason refs. close→satisfied when admitted ledger evidence fulfills exact-basis obligations. yield→indeterminate when the edge stays lawful and admitted progress/waiting does not decide, with resume basis naming what would decide. retry(defeated)→falsified only when admissible evidence defeats this attempt while the action stays lawful; all other retry is retry(undecided)→indeterminate, naming the deciding re-attempt. Repair requires coherent governing relation/basis/binding and a local defect permitting repair of the same edge: repair(implementation)→falsified for admitted implementation failure with failing obligation counterexample; every other repair is repair(proof)→indeterminate with repaired proof needed to decide. re-enter requires upstream asset/governing-relation change: undeclared needed relation/capability/authority→out_of_frame, naming it and its owner; otherwise unsupporting/stale/substituted/unrepairable basis→invalid_basis. reprice→out_of_frame for an undeclared selected outcome/bound, naming it, owner and requested constitutional re-entry. block(undeclared)→out_of_frame and block(basis)→invalid_basis when the action leaves the edge unable to proceed for the respective cause. Cause comes from reproducible basis/reason refs and adds no decision or core value.

grounding.quote:
`repair(proof)` is `indeterminate`, because a
defective proof leaves the edge's obligations undecided, while
`local_repair` is `falsified`, because the local defect defeats
acceptance of the candidate. `re-enter(undeclared)` is `out_of_frame`,
because the change needs a relation, capability or authority that no
admitted basis declares, while `re_enter` is `invalid_basis`. Neither
value counts toward the other's predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).

constraints.statement: Do not combine candidate availability, edge fulfillment, next-action selectability or candidate acceptance as each other's results. Closure repair is not ACTIVATION local_repair, and re-enter is not re_enter: proof repair is indeterminate versus local_repair falsified; undeclared re-entry is out_of_frame versus re_enter invalid_basis. In ODD §§11.5D, 16 and 19, disposition denotes a closure decision or, for typed no-action disposition, evaluate_next selection, never ACTIVATION §3 disposition. RELEASE §9 owns successor-claim dispositions. Repair/re-entry realization is a published graph action chosen by evaluate_next from admitted closure truth; evaluate_action's conceptual disposition does not itself invoke it.

grounding.quote:
A10 Liveness does not close semantic truth. Liveness observes activity,
inactivity, process state and interruption. It can support yield or a
liveness interruption; it cannot by itself declare semantic failure,
semantic closure or requirement non-satisfaction (P6).

constraints.statement: Yield requires the same edge/attempt to remain lawful, admitted progress/waiting, replay-visible resume basis and control return without failure classification. It preserves the current edge for long-running, bounded or partially productive work and is not retry, block, timeout or a local CLI loop. Liveness alone cannot establish semantic failure, closure, requirement non-satisfaction or retry(defeated). It can support yield or interruption.

conditions: For every closure decision, next-action selection and governing admitted/replay-derived carrier or projection.

grounding.quote:
A13 requires that the decision be reproducible from the inputs;
A13a requires that each governing carrier or projection carry the predecessor refs
that make reproduction reachable without external joins. A broken
predecessor chain is non-replayable at the carrier level and therefore
fails A13 (P3, P4b).

constraints.statement: Reproduction must use RuntimeEventLog, execution basis, event-backed IntentLineage, ProductAssetModel publication basis/event refs, selected outcome identity/admitted bounded refs, GapPressureRow, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog, admitted evidence, ledger, closure decision, NextActionBasis and visible policy refs. Inability to reproduce signals hidden state. Each governing carrier must carry causal predecessor refs: outcome/bounded refs→binding; lineage→model→gap→binding→priority→selected-action projection→construction intent→evidence→ledger→closure decision→next-action basis→post-action projection. Both projection occurrences must be predecessor-reachable; the latter also uses fresh eval_gap. Construction intent preserves authority refs. Reproduction must be reachable without external joins; a broken chain fails replayability.

exceptions: Intentionally opaque internals remain one bounded action and may compute an internal result with local control flow.

grounding.quote:
Once a refinement is published as graph structure,
the loop governs it recursively (P4a, P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Each published inner-vector boundary must obey all four functions with its own visible model, gap, binding, action, evidence, ledger, closure and next-action projection. Opaque internals may not publish, dispatch, retry, repair, re-enter or close graph work as a hidden traversal controller. ABG owns runtime truth/replay, graph-call lifecycle, actor/process supervision, continuation and re-entry mechanics. Product owns domain asset/catalogue meaning, gap interpretation and priority policy. DESIGN_MODULE tier 3 governs realization modules inside this split and may not fragment eval_gap/evaluate_next/evaluate_action into module-local authorities.

conditions: For any ticket, design, code module or proof touching the four functions, traversal, gap evaluation, selection, intent, worker invocation, evidence admission, fulfillment, liveness, closure, re-entry, public query or live proof.
exceptions: Unchanged accepted relations cite their accepted basis and are not proved again.

grounding.quote:
the causally
applicable members of this axiom set and the constitutional equation below
are the controlling acceptance constraints for the selected Product
outcome and the affected published boundary. Unchanged accepted relations
cite their accepted basis and are not proved again. The axiom family
authorises no horizontal realisation growth, creates no Product work and
does not widen the selected outcome (P6, P2).

constraints.statement: Causally applicable axioms and the constitutional equation control acceptance for the selected outcome and affected published boundary; they authorize no horizontal realization growth, new Product work or outcome widening. Local checklists, test names, source-grep checks, CLI summaries and implementation notes cannot weaken them. A locally complete ticket leaving a rival traversal-consequence path requires lawful re-entry, keeping the gap as blocker, or separately bounded paydown under an independently selected outcome/prerequisite. Correctness requires the next-work decision to derive only from the equation, with U=(selected outcome, optional admitted bounded basis) causally reachable through binding and intent. The equation projects lineage, synthesizes model, observes gap, binds U, evaluates initial selection, distinctly admits intent, invokes and admits evidence, evaluates action, refreshes model/gap/binding, derives post-action basis and evaluates next; unresolved post_reprice returns typed no-action.

grounding.quote:
If any of them conflicts with the admitted `EdgeFulfillmentLedger`,
`EdgeClosureDecision` or `NextActionProjection`, the ledger, decision and
projection chain wins. If that chain is absent, the edge has not
constitutionally closed and the next action has not been constitutionally
selected (P6).

constraints.statement: Gap dossiers, postflight/assurance reports, materialization manifests, liveness projections, run summaries, worker prose, screen/PTY transcripts, prompt packages, harness target arguments, source-grep tests, CLI output/branches, queries/gaps views and service outputs provide only evidence, diagnostics or read-model context; none independently closes an edge, selects work or routes retry/repair/re-entry. The admitted ledger/decision/projection chain prevails over conflicts; without it there is no constitutional edge closure or next-action selection. Public query may render read-only eval_gap/evaluate_action/evaluate_next outputs but cannot append events, invoke workers, admit intent, run evaluate_action or choose traversal itself.

grounding.quote:
If the team cannot explain the manual traversal, the automation is not yet
method-safe. Automation that cannot be explained in these terms is ahead
of the method (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Automation must stay true to the manual process, which an operator using only declared surfaces should be able to follow. It cannot skip undeclared nodes, fabricate authority, collapse multiple constitutional transitions into an opaque step without declared refinement, depend on implementation-carrier knowledge the installed product should lack, or merge installed-builder and development-product authority during self-host work. Inability to explain manual traversal means automation is not yet method-safe.

grounding.quote:
A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,
fail-closed and naming the violated rule, exactly as a typed asset is
enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Agents work from the smallest sufficient declared packet with source refs, not stale memory or wholesale hidden context. Compression is prompt input, never deciding authority; generic derived frames may orient precedence/re-entry/traceability but product behavior must come from current Product authority. Produced work must have correct change class, traceability and admission. Tickets, change classifications, design derivations and execution contracts must pass existing SPEC_METHOD/TICKETS admission: deterministic, fail-closed and naming violated rules, never treating a drafted classification as automatic truth. F_P reasons/drafts/proposes; F_D decides artifact conformance. A passed admission and completed walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification; repeated use cannot amend shared method or constitutionalize grey work.

grounding.quote:
An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

constraints.statement: A walkthrough stopping point is a method defect only when a competent, correctly configured agent using declared authority still cannot decide because an owning surface has ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or undecidable change class; reprice that defect into its owner. Ignored authority, stale memory or bad reasoning is agent error instead; malformed artifacts are rejected either way. Process-followability proof is independent of automated runtime: external API overload or transport failure cannot prove process soundness, because runtime availability and process validity differ.

conditions: The specified identities apply to the boundary.

grounding.quote:
No CLI, SDK, service, adapter, plugin, fixture, query or projection may
become a rival traversal controller. The consumer owns the concrete test
and evidence mechanism; this section owns the property that mechanism
must prove (P6).

constraints.statement: Negative proof must not manufacture the refusal, blocked event, gap or verdict being tested. The supported path is public entry → admitted GTL composition owning topology → named GraphFunction callable contract → implementation/plugin limited to admitted seam → ABG traversal/event/continuation/replay truth → replay projection → typed Product outcome/continuation. CLI, SDK, service, adapter, plugin, fixture, query and projection cannot become rival controllers. The consumer chooses the concrete test/evidence mechanism; the section fixes the property it must prove.

exceptions: A live requirement without an executable witness stops holding the enclosing carrier open when realized, explicitly deferred or explicitly repriced out of the active branch.

grounding.quote:
A product that publishes graph functions without this cumulative
environment law has a line that is graph-shaped but structurally wrong
(P4a, P6).

For current product closure, live current requirements that lack an
executable proof witness keep the enclosing carrier open until they are
realised, explicitly deferred, or explicitly repriced out of the active
branch. For the active software line the immediate pressure is usually a
realised testcase or archived test evidence, but the governing law is
proof-lane aware: the witness must be a governed realised proof surface
appropriate to the requirement class (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Published graph functions must obey cumulative-environment law rather than last-output-to-next-input wiring; explicit requires/provides/carries declarations remain a should. Local green arcs alone do not establish global closure: refined chains must lawfully close, preserve coarse contracts and agree across zoom. Live current requirements lacking appropriate executable proof keep the enclosing carrier open subject only to realization, explicit deferral or explicit repricing out of the active branch.

conditions: Installed proof applies where an installable development form exists; mandatory graph-function construction applies where the product provides ODD framework behavior.

grounding.quote:
Direct source checks stay useful and do not
replace installed-dev proof (P6, P3).

The product should be developed through the same graph-native method it
claims to provide. Where the product provides ODD framework behaviour, it
must build that behaviour through ODD graph functions and must not merely
publish ODD-shaped artifacts after imperative execution has already
decided the work.

constraints.statement: Direct source checks do not replace decisive isolated installed-dev proof. Developing the product through its own graph-native method is recommended generally. Building provided ODD framework behavior through ODD graph functions is mandatory; publishing ODD-shaped artifacts after imperative execution decided the work is prohibited.

conditions: Any listed failure is sufficient for violation of this profile.
constraints.statement: Violations are: a claimed step lacking node/vector; function lacking clear outer contract; automation not describable as manual traversal; installed-product dependence on authoring-carrier knowledge absent from clean targets; scenarios unable to name significant proving paths; closure without target-relative evidence; wiring bypassing cumulative environment; zoom disagreement; service-owned operative transition lacking published function outcome contract; workspace-first framework orchestration labeled GTL afterward; imperative closure/continuation/semantic-target movement/lineage truth outside declared graph-function, ABG or Product carriers; hidden execution authority in product/plugin for traversal, actor invocation, process supervision, retry, continuation, runtime events, projection or closure folds; flattening lawful yield into retry/block/timeout/local waiting/hidden CLI loop; query/postflight/service/operator decisions outside the constructive loop; or inability to follow the constitutional process end-to-end from declared authority, or acceptance of a constitutional artifact without deterministic admission.
constraints.uncertainty: The agentic inability condition is read with §11.7A's explicit distinction between qualified method defects and agent error.

grounding.quote:
The instruction does not mean starting from imperative scripts and adding
GTL words later, treating graph functions as documentation wrappers, or
letting service code become the hidden real carrier (P0, P6).

Operative framework behaviour must be built outcome-first: outcome
traversals first, declarative GTL/ABG carrier structure second, minimal
imperative adapter code last.

constraints.statement: Outcome traversals precede declarative GTL/ABG structure, which precedes minimal imperative adapter code. The invocation sequence cannot be replaced by imperative scripts later relabeled GTL, graph functions used as documentation wrappers or service code acting as hidden carrier. The canonical compression owns no determination; a differing source section decides.

conditions: An LLM is ramping into an ODD product.

grounding.quote:
If those questions cannot be answered quickly, the product is not yet
sufficiently ODD-shaped (P0, P2).

constraints.statement: The LLM should quickly recover: semantic source-to-outcome chain; typed domain assets/nodes; public functions; catalogue and GTL locations; ABG/Product ownership split; projection/query lane; each projection's admitted source and structural-drift fail-closed behavior; proof execution authority has not escaped ABG; constructive loop; closure vocabulary and replay-visible yield; capability-closing proof surfaces; outer carrier kept open by live unproved requirements despite inner green lanes; and whether an agent can follow declared authority alone with deterministic artifact admission. If these cannot be answered quickly, the product is not yet sufficiently ODD-shaped.

grounding.quote:
Use a post when the content is provisional, investigative, comparative,
argumentative or not yet ratified (P6).

Do not use a post for live requirements, live design decisions or active
process law. Those belong in the applicable bound WHAT surfaces or the
ratified design surfaces (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Posts carry provisional, investigative, comparative, argumentative or unratified content. Live requirements, live design decisions and active process law belong in applicable bound WHAT or ratified design surfaces and must not be carried as posts. Location, visibility and Closed state cannot confer ticket, Product, requirement or design authority.

grounding.quote:
1. State whether the post describes current reality, target direction or
   both (P1).
2. Keep findings separate from recommendations (P6).
3. Make claims with exact file or requirement references (P3, P6).
4. Do not present a post as if it were already ratified (P6).
5. Do not rewrite closed history by stealth. An open post may be revised
   in place; a closed post should normally be superseded by a new post
   (P4b, P3).
6. Keep each post to one bounded subject (P2).

constraints.statement: Each post uses one listed category and the base template, with a MATRIX decision table replacing central free prose. It must identify current reality, target direction or both; separate findings from recommendations; support claims with exact file/requirement refs; avoid presenting itself as ratified; preserve closed history against stealth rewriting; and concern one bounded subject. Its subject should be short, specific and stable enough for later scanning. Default file carriers use the prescribed timestamp/category/subject filename; non-file carriers must retain equivalent identity/history fields. Status explicitly records discussion state.

grounding.quote:
A post becomes consequential only when its content is explicitly adopted
into a bound WHAT surface, ratified design or accepted implementation.
Until then it is commentary, not law (P6).

A post that carries such evidence or proposes such a change does not
adopt it (§9) (P6).

constraints.statement: Post content becomes consequential only through explicit adoption into bound WHAT, ratified design or accepted implementation. Closing a discussion is not adoption. Carrying incident/review evidence or proposing reusable method change does not adopt it; STDO-UP-012 propagation remains governed by SPEC_METHOD §6.

exceptions: A directory may contain multiple definitions only when it contains multiple distinct product WHATs.

grounding.quote:
Every product defined under this method publishes one JSON definition for
each distinct current product WHAT. Its conventional filename is
`stdo_<label>.json`; `stdo_default.json` is the default for a source
project with one product definition. A directory may hold more than one
definition when it hosts more than one distinct product WHAT, and only
then. Several build tenants realising the same WHAT are entries in one definition and
never add definition files (P3).

constraints.statement: Publish exactly one JSON definition per distinct current WHAT; additional tenants of the same WHAT are entries, never additional definitions. A definition identity may persist across successive releases; forks, replacements or independently governed WHATs require another definition_id. Immutable Product/release identities remain separate. Product-definition, immutable Product, bounded-context and tenant identity URIs remain subject to IDENTITY and owning authority; URI, filename, path, label or proximity creates/widens no identity or authority. Relative refs resolve from retrieval URI, not assumed source-project proximity. Overlay/schema/template own only locator/relation shape, never referenced content.

conditions: For every Product Definition.
exceptions: product.bounded_context is null if no separate enclosing context is claimed; sprint bindings are optional.

grounding.quote:
- `composition`: explicit relations to other product definitions; and
- `$schema` and `kind`: the schema locator and the
  `stdo.product-definition` discriminator.

constraints.statement: Each definition contains product identity/display name/source locator/explicit enclosing context or null; constitution.stdo source repository, mutable discovery selector and exact installed basis/deterministic manifest digest; every non-STDO set in additional_authorities; basis-qualified entrypoints; agent_bootstrap entrypoint and marker-managed targets; local axioms/overrides/disambiguations with owner/target/basis/scope and applicable context resolution; one or more accepted reference_frame_bases with authorities/scopes; current what Intent/Product/specification bindings; how shared surfaces and one or more independent tenants; ticketing Goals/tickets/comments/optional sprints; explicit composition; $schema and kind=stdo.product-definition. Repeating source truth in JSON is non-conformant rival authority. product.bounded_context identifies only enclosing WHAT context, not an exhaustive registry or flattened subordinate/peer/composed/tenant/user/runtime namespace; local disambiguations name their exact contexts.

conditions: The family consequences use the declared instance premises, not foundational commitments alone.

grounding.quote: Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does

constraints.statement: F12 consequences preserve project-owned WHAT and layout without becoming part of the method; one locating definition per WHAT without repeated content; separate definition/Product/release/tenant/project identities and explicit verified composition; exactly one applicable discovered definition or fail closed; complete constitutional sufficiency without entrypoint replacement or design-invented Product meaning; one exact complete immutable release verified before use, owner acceptance of exact change plans, and fail-closed unverifiable state with prior state kept/recovered; exactly one context-qualified material meaning after authorized resolution; imports preserving owner meaning and authority, with changed applicability rebound and missing meaning/adoption/authority reported before reliance; Product-admitted frame engagement with availability/adoption/activation and frame/actor/lineage identities distinct; one tenant registry and separate Goals/ticket/comment authorities; one owner per law, members governing together as one release, source-condition/digest-preserving derived surfaces stale on source change, digest equality proving identity not fidelity; and bootstrap from the selected release template into existing surfaces without a rival local method root, with initial requirements from any legitimate constitutional input. Each consumer applies only its owner's rule. Widening Product scope to executable tool/runtime/realization requires separate explicit human authorization.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed foundational standing, referenced rule implementations and external consumer loci are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The STDO basis identifies one complete
immutable RC cut and its exact installed-release manifest, never a
hand-selected subset. Each `constitution.entrypoints[]` member names the
basis against which its URI resolves. Entry points are derived navigation
and can neither narrow nor replace a complete selected constitution (P3,
P6).

constraints.statement: The complete governing set must collectively recover all five dimensions for its scope. constitution.stdo.basis locates one complete immutable RC cut and exact installed manifest, never a selected subset; additional_authorities locates every additional set/source. Each entrypoint names its resolving basis and cannot narrow/replace the set. Product-meaning ontology belongs in or is cited by bound WHAT. Accepted realization design ontology has semantic-design authority only for its boundary, derives from WHAT and applicable methods, and cannot invent missing Product meaning.

grounding.quote:
Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status
and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8
JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line
endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path
order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible
rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).

It uses the same
canonical JSON hashing rule. Already-installed status supplies no
additional authority and does not change the digest. Mutation requires
explicit acceptance of this exact plan and re-derives it; possession of its
digest alone grants no operation authority.

constraints.statement: Canonical plan hashing uses UTF-8 JSON, recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF endings and one final LF. Basis-only Adoption Plans exclude machine-local installation paths/status; fleet plans order by deterministic discovery path. Complete update uses the same serialization but additionally binds physical destinations/preimages and selected cohort/routes/source observations. Already-installed status changes neither its digest nor authority. Digest possession alone never grants operation authority; mutation requires explicit acceptance and exact re-derivation.

grounding.quote:
`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.
`constitution.stdo.selector` is a mutable `stdo://channels/<version>`
discovery selector whose alias semantics are owned by the release law (the
[RELEASE](RELEASE.md) member). Neither is operative authority.

are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Only constitution.stdo.basis.uri and manifest_sha256 author STDO selection; transport repository and mutable channel selector do not. Every manager-owned component from configured store root downward must be a physical directory or regular file of declared type. Symlinks, junctions, reparse points, devices, sockets, other redirections/special entries fail closed. Verification inventories all entry types including directories, rejects entries not derived from exact manifest file paths and never follows unmanifested aliases. No cache, registry, checkout, alias, schema or agent file may silently replace the selected basis. Every case-insensitively parsed stdo: schema locator must name that same immutable cut before schema loading.

grounding.quote:
- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit
  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound
  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes
  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses
  mutation;
- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with
  respect to Product Definitions; and
